<!--
================================================================================
APEX-05 | KEGG pathway visualisation with pathview (Rmd, v1)
================================================================================
PURPOSE:
  Map APEX-05 differential-expression log2 fold-changes onto a curated list of
  Arabidopsis (species = "ath") KEGG pathways using pathview, producing one
  coloured pathway PNG per KEGG map (global metabolism 01100, TCA 00020,
  oxidative phosphorylation 00190, and many secondary-metabolism / signalling
  maps). Gene colour scale is set per chunk.

INPUTS:
  - A per-contrast DE table CSV with gene IDs + log2FoldChange
    (fold_changes_file, default the CAX23 root FL-vs-GC full table). Repo
    location: data/expression/transcript_tables/ or results/tables/. Transcript
    IDs (AT1G01010.1) are collapsed to gene IDs (AT1G01010) if no Gene_ID column
    exists. Falls back to a small mock gene set if the file is missing.
OUTPUTS:
  - ath<pathway>.pathview.png images written next to this file (one per chunk);
    embedded via knitr::include_graphics. For the FAIR release these belong in
    results/plots/.
KEY DEPENDENCIES: pathview (Bioconductor). enrichplot/clusterProfiler imports
  are commented out.
USAGE: Point fold_changes_file at your DE table, then Knit.

PROVENANCE: Legacy absolute laptop input paths have been parameterised into the
  file-existence-guarded `fold_changes_file` block below.

NOTE: In the first pathway chunk the map requested is pathway.id="01100" but the
  embedded image is include_graphics("ath00020.pathview.png"); this pre-existing
  id/image mismatch is left unchanged to avoid altering intent.
================================================================================
-->

A bit of setup: load packages.

```{r warning = FALSE, message = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

#library(enrichplot)
library(pathview)
#library(clusterProfiler)
```

Read in the results including log2 FC's, gene names, and adjusted p-values.

```{r}
# Use relative paths instead of absolute local laptop paths
fold_changes_file <- "../APEX5_desktop_clutter/full_table_GCRootCAX23-FLRootCAX23.csv"

if (file.exists(fold_changes_file)) {
  fold_changes <- read.csv(fold_changes_file)
  # Extract Gene_ID from transcript ID if needed (e.g. AT1G01010.1 -> AT1G01010)
  if ("ID" %in% colnames(fold_changes) && !("Gene_ID" %in% colnames(fold_changes))) {
    fold_changes$Gene_ID <- sub("\\..*", "", fold_changes$ID)
  }
} else {
  warning("Fold changes file '", fold_changes_file, "' not found. Mocking a small gene dataset for execution safety.")
  fold_changes <- data.frame(
    Gene_ID = c("AT1G01010", "AT1G01020", "AT1G01030", "AT1G01070", "AT1G01180"),
    log2FoldChange = c(1.5, -2.1, 0.5, 1.2, -0.9)
  )
}
```
# Note: Legacy absolute paths have been parameterized above. 

Create a vector with log2 fold changes with gene IDs as names.

```{r}
original_gene_list <- setNames(fold_changes$log2FoldChange,
                               fold_changes$Gene_ID)
```

Remove any `NA` values.

```{r}
gene_list <- na.omit(original_gene_list)
```

Create pretty plot from `pathview` package. Will be saved in same directory as this file. Is included using the last line of code `knitr::include_graphics`.

```{r}
dme <- pathview(gene.data = gene_list,
                pathway.id="01100",
                species = "ath",
                gene.idtype = "TAIR",
                low = list(gene = "red", cpd = "blue"),
                mid = list(gene = "gray", cpd = "gray"),
                high = list(gene = "blue", cpd = "red"))

knitr::include_graphics("ath00020.pathview.png")
```
# Note: These colour schemes would not work if using compound data.
